**Answer to your question:**

The other blur test ("shows invalid email error on blur") doesn't need this treatment because it triggers the blur by clicking a plain `<textarea>` (Message), not a `<button type="submit">`. Moving focus onto a plain input only needs `mousedown` to land — that alone fires the blur/focus swap the test relies on. A submit button's actual effect (form submission) only fires on a *completed* click (`mousedown` **and** `mouseup` on the same element), so it's the only element that can be defeated by a layout shift happening mid-click. Every other e2e test I found that clicks a submit-style button (`newgame.spec.ts`, `mailout.spec.ts`, `responses.spec.ts`, `drinkers.spec.ts`, `moregames.spec.ts`) does so after filling *valid* data, so no validation error renders on blur, no layout shifts, and the click lands cleanly — this hazard only exists where you deliberately submit *invalid/empty* data and expect an error to appear right as you click.

I grepped the rest of `e2e/*.spec.ts` for the same shape (fill invalid/empty → immediately click a submit-type button expecting a validation error) and found no other occurrences — `info.spec.ts` was the only one.

The two other failures that showed up in the full suite run (`responses.spec.ts` on firefox, `newgame.spec.ts` on mobile) are unrelated: both passed cleanly on isolated re-run, confirming they're pre-existing nondeterministic flakes (the `responses.spec.ts` file even has its own documented SSE-refresh race workaround already), not the deterministic click-miss bug I found and fixed.
